analyses.failure: test_chk_014_nominal_latency — CHK-013: i_full_thr=depth expected o_full_thr=0 got 1 at 1680691 ps (fails only in runs with the metastability model on: base.s1-s5, cell1/3/4, macro, wr_slow, rd_slow; passes in model_off.s1, syn.s1 and small.s1, see results.json:37-50)
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:524 CHK-013 (c): "if i_full_thr==PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_full_thr == (o_full AND i_rst_n_sw AND NOT o_sw_rst_busy)". rules.json:659 (REQ-FUNC-010): "o_full_thr shall be 1 when the write-domain occupancy estimate is greater than or equal to i_full_thr ... it is pessimistic for the full side". spec:137 REQ-FUNC-008: the full flag "shall never be 0 while the FIFO is physically full". Metastability model, spec:653 (rules.json:5481 AF-10.6.4-01): "Each bit of the synchronized vector is independent. When a bit changes at the input of the last stage, the model chooses ... an extra delay of 0, 1, or 2 destination cycles." spec:684 then claims: "A Gray pointer changes one bit per update, so a late bit makes the destination domain see the previous pointer value for a while instead of the new one." The spec example uses updates "six source cycles apart" (spec:653). It never covers back-to-back pointer updates.
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:106 w_full_n = (reg_wgray == w_rgray_s ^ MSK); :120 w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s (4-bit, modulo 16); :125 o_full = w_wr_blk | w_full_n; :126 o_full_thr = w_wr_blk ? (i_full_thr==0) : (w_occ >= i_full_thr). If w_rgray_s is a real past value of the read Gray pointer, w_occ>=8 only when w_occ==8, which equals w_full_n, so (c) holds. m_vlsit_afifo_sync.sv:46-56 makes one independent m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync per bit. m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 picks a random 0..2 extra delay for each bit separately (:160-169), and a new change replaces a pending one and restarts the delay. When the read pointer moves at consecutive read edges (6 ns read clock against a 14 ns write clock in this run, log base.s1:47), a later bit change can come out before an earlier one. Then w_rgray_s is a value the read pointer never had. Its binary w_rbin_s can be ahead of the true read pointer, or even ahead of reg_wbin. w_occ then wraps to 9..15, which gives o_full_thr=1 while w_full_n=0, o_sw_rst_busy=0 and i_rst_n_sw=1. That is the failing sample. This is inferred from the code: no waveform of w_rgray_s is available.
analyses.test_does: test_async_gray_fifo.py:845-890. Env(ft=DEPTH=8, et=0). In each of 10 rounds: one write into the empty FIFO, a fill to 8 words (:873-879), one read at Tr (:882-885), then drain() (:463-471), which reads on consecutive read edges whenever o_empty=0. In model-on runs it marks only the exact-latency part not verifiable (:855-856, log base.s1:48); the per-edge assertions stay on. The write monitor's _on_w (:196-202) evaluates CHK-013(c) at every write edge with exp = int(full==1 and sw==1 and busy==0) and asserted fth==exp. The sample had o_full=0 and o_full_thr=1.

candidates.evidence_for: The RTL model does exactly what spec:653 and AF-10.6.4-01 say (independent per-bit 0..2 extra cycles, pending change replaced). The spec's claim at spec:684 that only "the previous pointer value" is seen holds only when updates are further apart than the delay window. The spec example uses updates six source cycles apart. With back-to-back updates, an independent per-bit delay of up to 2 cycles lets bit changes from different source cycles reorder. That conflicts with REQ-FUNC-008/009/010 (pessimistic flags) and with TEST-008 (spec:1246, "flags never optimistic"). The failure follows the model: it appears in every model-on run and never in model_off.s1 or syn.s1 (results.json:37-50). The same symptom shows in other tests with the model on (base.s3.log:12532, base.s5.log:10068).
candidates.evidence_against: One could read 'metastability model' as implying only physically possible behaviour: a real 2-FF synchronizer delays a bit by at most about one cycle and cannot reorder bit changes launched in different source cycles. Under that reading, the RTL model, not the spec, is at fault.

candidates.evidence_for: The model in rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 can make the synchronized Gray vector take a value the source never held. No real synchronizer does that. The FIFO logic in m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:106/120/126 trusts the synchronized pointer to be a past source value. If the designer intends the model to be physically realistic, this file is the defect. It is RTL deliverable code (FEAT-009).
candidates.evidence_against: The datapath and flag logic (wr.sv:106-126) are correct for any coherent synchronized pointer. The model follows the spec wording literally. model_off.s1 and syn.s1 pass this test, so the FIFO logic itself is not shown to be wrong.

candidates.evidence_for: contract.json:559-560 defines CHK-014 with the metastability model off, yet the test also runs in model-on runs. It only marks the latency part not verifiable (:855-856).
candidates.evidence_against: The failing check is CHK-013, an always-on assertion (contract.json:524, 'At every rising edge of i_clk_wr'). The test computes it correctly from the contract. The same CHK-013 violation appears in other tests with the model on, so skipping CHK-014 in those runs would not remove it.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify the spec, section 10.6.4/REQ-VER-001: state whether the model must keep the synchronized vector coherent, i.e. always a value the source held. For example: the extra delay is chosen per vector update, or bit changes from different source cycles may not reorder, or at most 1 extra cycle. Or state that the model may produce incoherent values, and then define what REQ-FUNC-008/009/010 require under it. (2) If coherence is required, fix the RTL model in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 so an output change can never overtake an earlier pending change. One way: share one delay decision per synchronizer vector in m_vlsit_afifo_sync, or hold later changes until earlier pending ones are released. Then rerun the model-on runs. (3) Keep CHK-013(c) as written. Separately, consider gating CHK-014's latency part to model-off runs only, as the contract states. Do not relax CHK-013.

analyses.failure: test_chk_015_model_latency_window — CHK-015: o_full=1 at once after the refill got 0 (all 14 runs, including model_off.s1 and syn.s1)
analyses.spec_says: contract.json:582 CHK-015 stimulus: "at least 100 isolated single reads from a full FIFO (refill after each), with random gaps of at least 6 destination edges". contract.json:583 expected: "For every isolated read, o_full falls after write edge L with L in {2,3,4}". The local-write full behaviour is in contract.json:561 (CHK-014): "After the 8th write edge, o_full=1 at once". REQ-FUNC-008 is at spec:137.
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:109 accepts a write when ~w_full_n; :134 increments reg_wbin; :138/:153 update reg_wgray at the same edge; :106/:125 o_full = w_full_n is combinational from the local reg_wgray. The write that brings the FIFO to 8 words therefore makes o_full=1 at the next sample. On the read side, m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:100 accepts a read at every read edge where i_rd_en=1 and o_empty=0, and :126 advances the read pointer. If i_rd_en stays 1, the RTL keeps draining the FIFO. That is correct behaviour.
analyses.test_does: iso_reads (test_async_gray_fifo.py:670-696): it fills to DEPTH, then for each iteration calls `j = await env.rstep(1)` (:683). rstep (:297-300) sets i_rd_en=1 and never clears it. The test then goes to the write side (:686-687 wsync and wait_dst for LMAX+4 write edges) without `rstep(0)`, so i_rd_en stays 1 and more reads are accepted on every following read edge. The scoreboard counts them correctly. After that it writes one refill word (:691) and asserts o_full==1 at the next write edge (:694). The FIFO now holds about 8 - k + 1 < 8 words, so o_full=0 is correct. Compare iso_writes (:664-666) and CHK-014 (:882-885), which both call `rstep(0)` right after the single read. The failure is in the first iso_reads iteration, right after the 100 iso_writes (base.s1.log:1257-1264, about 24 us of iso_writes).

candidates.evidence_for: i_rd_en is left at 1 after the 'isolated' read (test :683, rstep at :297-300 never restores 0). The sibling helpers clear it (:666, :885). The failure is identical in every configuration, including model_off.s1 and syn.s1 (results.json:78-91), where the crossing latency is exact and the model plays no part. CHK-017 uses the same iso_reads and fails at the same line in model_off and syn (model_off.s1.log:1748, syn.s1.log:1789). The RTL full logic is local and immediate (wr.sv:106,125). It is the same logic CHK-014 checks at :879 and passes in model_off.s1.
candidates.evidence_against: No waveform in hand directly shows several reads accepted after the isolated read. That part is inferred from the code: i_rd_en is never driven back to 0 before :694.

candidates.evidence_for: A write-pointer or full-compare bug would also give o_full=0 after a write that should fill the FIFO.
candidates.evidence_against: The full compare (wr.sv:35,106) is correct for Gray pointers. For example, wbin=13 and rbin=5 give gray 1011 == 0111^1100. The same 'o_full=1 at once after the 8th write' check passes in CHK-014 with the model off (test :879; model_off.s1 CHK-014 passed, results.json:42).

candidates.evidence_for: The contract says 'isolated single reads' but does not say how i_rd_en must be driven between them.
candidates.evidence_against: 'Isolated single read' plus 'refill after each' clearly means one accepted read per iteration. No reasonable reading allows a continuous drain.

analyses.options: Fix the test: in iso_reads, add `await env.rstep(0)` right after `j = await env.rstep(1)` (test :683), as in iso_writes :666 and CHK-014 :885. Optionally also assert that exactly one read was accepted before the refill (len(env.Q)==DEPTH-1). No RTL or spec change is indicated. Note that after this fix, model-on runs may still show the coherence issue described for CHK-014/CHK-016.

analyses.spec_says: contract.json:287 CHK-003 (b): "If i_empty_thr >= PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH, then o_empty_thr=1." rules.json:686 (REQ-FUNC-010): "o_empty_thr shall be 1 when the read-domain occupancy estimate is less than or equal to i_empty_thr ... pessimistic ... for the empty side (it can be smaller)". spec:138 REQ-FUNC-009: the empty flag "shall never be 0 while the FIFO is physically empty". contract.json:606-607 CHK-016: the model is on in some runs and "CHK-001..CHK-013 never fail". Model definition at spec:653 (per-bit independent 0..2 extra cycles); spec:684 claims only the previous pointer value is seen.
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:112 w_occ = w_wbin_s - reg_rbin (4-bit, modulo 16); :118 o_empty_thr = w_rd_blk ? 1 : (w_occ <= i_empty_thr). With i_empty_thr=13 (log base.s1.log:1268), o_empty_thr=0 needs w_occ in {14,15}, i.e. the synchronized write pointer is 1-2 entries behind the local read pointer. With a coherent, monotonic w_wgray_s that cannot happen: :97/:100 accept a read only when reg_rgray != w_wgray_s, so reg_rbin <= w_wbin_s. It can happen when m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 delays bits of w_wgray_s independently. A later bit change can show first, so w_wbin_s jumps ahead (an optimistic, non-real pointer), the reader advances on it, and then the delayed bit arrives and w_wbin_s steps back below reg_rbin. In that window w_empty_n=0, so o_empty=0 on a FIFO the read side has over-read. This is inferred from the code. The Python CHK-006/CHK-005 scoreboard did not fire first only because CHK-003 is evaluated earlier in _on_r (test :238-244).
analyses.test_does: test :922-950. Random clock pair, here 10/10.3 ns. Thresholds ft=10, et=13 are random (:927). Random traffic with burst fill/drain and up to 100% read density (:511-536, Traffic :402-429). _on_r (:241-242) asserts eth==1 whenever i_empty_thr >= DEPTH and i_rst_n_rd=1, as CHK-003(b) requires. In model_off/syn runs the test fails at its first read edge: Env.start (:146-160) starts the monitors (:157-158) with sb_on=True (:122) and an empty Q before hw_reset() (:160) resets the DUT. The DUT was left non-empty by the failed CHK-015 (i_rd_en held, FIFO partly full), so the first read edge sees o_empty=0 with Q empty and raises CHK-006 (:266).

candidates.evidence_for: The mid-test failure appears only in model-on runs (base.s1, base.s2). base.s5 passes (results.json:125). The RTL flag logic is correct for any coherent synchronized pointer. The incoherent pointer comes from a model that implements spec:653 literally (independent per-bit delay, pending replacement). The spec's own reasoning at spec:684 ignores back-to-back pointer updates, which CHK-016 drives at up to 100% density. So the spec's model rule conflicts with REQ-FUNC-009/010 and TEST-008 'flags never optimistic'.
candidates.evidence_against: If the designer intends the model to be physically realistic (no reordering of bit changes from different source cycles), the defect is in the RTL model file instead (see A).

candidates.evidence_for: rtl/m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-182 can produce synchronized Gray values the source never held. Real synchronizers cannot. The FIFO then becomes optimistic (o_empty=0 on an over-read FIFO), which REQ-FUNC-009 forbids. If the FIFO must stay safe under this model, the read logic would need to be robust to non-monotonic synchronized pointers, which is not standard.
candidates.evidence_against: rd.sv:97-118 matches REQ-FUNC-009/010 and the standard Gray FIFO design. The model follows the spec text.

candidates.evidence_for: In model_off.s1, syn.s1, cell3.s1 (and similar runs) the CHK-016 failure is a TB cascade. Monitors check with sb_on=True and empty Q before the DUT reset (test :122, :157-160), while the DUT still holds words from the failed CHK-015. The failure lands 12 ns into the test (model_off.s1.log:1581-1582).
candidates.evidence_against: The headline failure in base.s1 (and base.s2) is mid-test, after the hw reset and 12 us of clean checking, with a value (w_occ>=14) that only an incoherent synchronized pointer can produce. The CHK-003(b) check matches the contract.

analyses.options: (1) Clarify spec 10.6.4: must the synchronized vector stay coherent (per-update delay, no reordering, max +1 cycle)? Or are incoherent values allowed, and if so what flag guarantees apply? (2) If coherence is required, change the RTL model (m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv / m_vlsit_afifo_sync.sv) so a later bit change cannot overtake an earlier pending one, then rerun base.s1-s5. (3) Separately, fix the TB cascade that hides the real result in model_off/syn runs: start Env with sb_on=False (test :122) and enable checking only after hw_reset releases both resets (:170-171), or reset the DUT before starting the monitors. Also fix iso_reads (:683) so CHK-015 does not leave the FIFO dirty. Keep CHK-003(b) and CHK-032 as they are.
